charter:
# Charter — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

T5 delivers the kata capability: a procedure change is measured on a held-out instrument, adopted only when it wins, reverted when it regresses, and never approved by the actor that proposed it. The capability is built (migrations 0066_kata.sql and 0067_kata_gate.sql, the `kata.*` action family and its integration suites) and its project row is closed; this charter is the retrospective record the v4 close gate requires, not a claim of new construction.

The project's authority comes from SPEC_V2 §12's T5 row, and its boundaries are the ones the inception analysis set: the instruments belong to S16–S20, the lesson register to T8, the development project to T6, the andon cord to S06 and the tool platform to T13. The kata reuses the eval, benchmark and approval surfaces and defines none of them. Its acceptance is the six refusal scenarios of the delivered gate plus the three audit findings carried by the code unit; the receipt stays red until those land, and the closure review records that split openly.

The review is the Architecture Board's, under its published standing delegation; the tranche decision is the programme owner's. This charter claims no tranche authority and re-opens no delivered slice.

body.assignment: Deliver the architecture record for the kata capability: a procedure change measured on a held-out instrument, adopted only on a win, reverted on a regression, with the adoption decided by a person distinct from the kata's actor. The assignment is retrospective: the product shipped on issue #77 and the merges the closure review cites, and this statement records the architecture that shipped.
body.scope: The kata action family, the two kata migrations, the eval and approval reuse, and the seven A–D artefacts. Out of scope: the instruments, the lesson promotion, the development project, the andon cord and the tool platform. The phase set is A–D on the delivery ADM; the programme row carries adm_phase G and plateau capability.
body.responsibilities: The coach seat opens and measures; the kata owner sets the prediction and the instrument; the adoption approver decides keep or revert; the Architecture Board reviews the architecture record under its standing delegation; the programme owner decides the tranche. No role signs its own gate.
body.acceptance_criteria: The acceptance is A1–A8 of the acceptance document, each by its test, plus the closure review's outcome-vs-acceptance table. A1–A5 are delivered; A6–A8 are the code unit's and are named open. The statement claims no tranche authority: authorisation is the programme's separate act.
body.constraints: No second metric store, no second approval path, no second runtime or service, no direct database path from the kata, and no adoption by a non-human principal. The kata tenant is the systemic kata's home; the coached tenant is never the kata's tenant.
body.retrospective: This SoAW is authored at the 2026-11-28 retrospective snapshot against a closed project row. It describes what the delivered capability is, names the three open findings, and records that the tranche authorisation is the review's act rather than this document's.

Seven A–D artefacts for T5, the kata capability, at the 2026-11-28 retrospective snapshot. Phase A carries four PSA artefacts (a stakeholder matrix, two catalogs and a diagram); Phases B, C and D carry one HLD artefact each. An artefact with no link would be an orphan and is refused before the create.

This index is the pack's document for the architecture-artifact category. It records what the factory creates and how the set relates; the individual artefacts carry the substance. documents.title: User Stories — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# User stories

## Personas

The coach seat opens and measures a kata; the kata owner sets the prediction and the instrument; the adoption approver is a person distinct from the kata's actor and alone decides keep or revert; the programme owner reads the closure review; the instrument owner (S16–S20) supplies the eval or benchmark version the measurement runs on.
## Stories

As a coach, I want to open a kata only when there is a replayable flow and a recorded prediction, so that an unmeasurable guess never becomes work. As a kata owner, I want a candidate measured on the held-out split, so that the verdict is not fitted to the data it was chosen on. As an adoption approver, I want a keep-or-revert decision recorded against the measured baseline, so that a regression restores the base version. As a programme owner, I want the kata's outcome, measurement and decision in one audited record, so that the closure review reads evidence rather than a claim.
## Scenarios

Opening without an instrument is refused (`kata_open.rs`). A second kata for an open signature is refused (`kata_open.rs`). The measurement runs on the test split (`kata_measure.rs`). A measured regression reverts the candidate (`kata_revert.rs`). A flat or incomparable result adopts nothing (`kata_revert.rs`). The kata cannot approve its own adoption (`kata_adopt.rs`). A completed run pins the instrument it measured (`eval_instrument_digest.rs`, to create). A systemic kata opens under tenant kata (`kata_tenant.rs`, to create). A schema drift opens a kata with a contract-test instrument (`kata_drift.rs`, to create).
## Verify

Each scenario names its integration test in `crates/actions/tests/`. The five delivered tests exist at the baseline and are named in the acceptance-criteria document; the three carried by the code unit are marked to create there. A story whose scenario has no test is a gap the acceptance document records, not a completed story.

documents.title: Acceptance Criteria — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Acceptance criteria

## Scenarios

A1: a kata opens only with an instrument and a prediction. A2: one open kata per signature. A3: the measurement runs on the held-out split. A4: a regression reverts and a flat result adopts nothing. A5: the kata cannot approve its own adoption. A6: a completed eval run pins the digest of the instrument it measured. A7: a systemic kata is created under tenant kata with its own policy. A8: a 422 schema drift opens a kata with a contract-test instrument and a typed threshold.
## Verify commands

A1–A5: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test kata_open --test kata_measure --test kata_revert --test kata_adopt`. A6: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test eval_instrument_digest` (to create). A7: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test kata_tenant` (to create). A8: `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test kata_drift` (to create). The compile and lint verdict is the repository's preflight, not a local build.
## Results

A1–A5 pass at the delivered merges recorded in the closure review. A6–A8 are not yet exercised: the tests do not exist, the findings are open P1 packages, and the receipt's `T5-rework` check is red until they land. The closure review records this split explicitly rather than folding the open findings into a pass.
## Status

Delivered: A1–A5, on the evidence of the kata test suites and migrations 0066/0067. Open: A6–A8, carried by the code unit linked from this tranche. The project's acceptance against SPEC_V2 §12 is met on A1–A5; the programme's rework resolution is not, and the tranche exit waits for it.

documents.title: Definition of Ready — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Definition of ready

## Independent

A kata unit lands inside the kata action family and its tests; it does not need another unit's files. The real orderings are typed: the instrument comes from S16–S20 and the development handoff is T6, neither of which this project's units edit.
## Negotiable

The outcome is fixed by SPEC_V2 §12's T5 gate and the six refusal scenarios; the implementation of a new instrument class or a digest column is settled at delivery, not in this brief.
## Valuable

The outcome removes the named gap the register carries: an improvement that cannot be measured on the instrument it named, and a kata that could run inside the tenant it coaches. It maps to `B3` self-development and `B1` auditable decisions.
## Estimable

The baseline is `main@ea03b188a`, the files are named (the kata action family, migrations 0066/0067, the eval run row), and every acceptance command is a test target.
## Small

One unit is one issue, one branch and one PR; the three open findings are one code unit because they share the kata and eval surfaces and cannot merge independently of each other.
## Testable

Every scenario carries a `@verify` id and a test target; a scenario without a test is marked to create in the acceptance document rather than counted as passing.
## Dependencies

T5 needs P0, T2, S16, S17, S18, S19 and S20 (meta.depends_on). The kata loop reads their instruments; it redefines none of them. The three open findings depend on no other unit.

documents.title: Definition of Done — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Definition of done

## Acceptance criteria

One row per scenario A1–A8, each keyed by its test target. A unit is done only when every row has a result at the merge head; a green suite on a different revision is not the evidence.
## Evidence at completion

The command, its result and the merge SHA per row. A1–A5 carry the delivered merges and their suites; A6–A8 carry their tests once the code unit lands. Evidence recorded against a stale SHA is recomputed rather than cited.
## Repo gate

The repository's preflight is the compile and lint verdict; the PR's public CI is the final gate. No local compiling build is used as a gate, and no test is skipped to make the gate green.
## Merge and closure

One PR closes the unit's issue; the branch is deleted after the merge. A project closes only when its receipt is green at a pinned snapshot; the tranche exit reads that receipt, so an open P0/P1 rework package keeps the close honest and the exit red.

documents.title: Architecture Analysis — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Architecture and analysis pack

## Current state

The kata capability exists: migrations 0066 and 0067 create the kata, candidate, measurement and gate rows; the `kata.*` action family is registered and served; the test suites kata_open, kata_measure, kata_revert, kata_adopt, kata_gets, kata_union and kata_benchmark exercise the loop. The instrument is reused from S19: eval_version pins a drawn split and eval_run carries a variant and a change patch. The approvals surface is the shared row and policy.
## Options considered

The alternative to a kata aggregate was a benchmark-only improvement path, which cannot express a held-out adoption decision for an eval instrument; a second metric store was refused because the instrument is S16–S20's. Storing the instrument digest on the run row was chosen over minting a version on every edit because the run must identify what it measured even after the instrument moves.
## Risks

The inherited risk is that a measurement names an instrument that has since changed: R6's digest closes it. A systemic kata running inside the coached tenant is a cross-tenant risk: R7 closes it. A schema drift with no instrument is a silent patch risk: R8 closes it. Each risk has a test as its check, not a waiver.
## Dependency map

T5 depends on P0 (the programme and its tranches), T2 (the decision ladder), S16 (the inference ledger and prompt audit), S17 (the benchmark harness), S18 (the kata improvement loop), S19 (the eval builder) and S20 (the eval hillclimb). The edges are `needs` edges in the project row; none is open construction except S19's remaining lane.

documents.title: Architecture Design — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Architecture design

## Context and boundary

T5 owns the kata capability: open, analyse, propose, measure, adopt, propagate and close. It does not own the instruments (S16–S20), the lesson register (T8), the development project (T6), the andon cord (S06) or the tool platform (T13). The design keeps the kata in one action family and one store, and reuses the approval and instrument rows rather than copying them.
## Aggregates, tables and actions

The aggregates are the kata, the candidate, the measurement, the adoption and the propagation. Migrations 0066 and 0067 create the kata rows and the gate; `kata.*` actions write them. The adoption is an `approval` row decided by a human distinct from the kata's actor; the revert restores the recorded base version through the target's own publish action. The three open findings add no aggregate: a digest on eval_run, a tenant on the kata row and a contract-test instrument class.
## Decisions

The instrument is never defined by the kata; it is pinned by version. The split is held out at measure time, not judged after the fact. The adoption decision is a person's, recorded with the measurement it cites. A kata opens only for a replayable flow. These decisions are constraints and action refusals, not conventions.
## Acceptance

A1–A8 of the acceptance document, each by its test. The delivered five pass; the three open ones are the code unit's, and the closure review names them as open rather than folding them into the delivered gate.
## Architecture artefacts

The pack carries the seven A–D artefacts: the stakeholder map, the driver and requirements catalogs, the solution concept, the capability map, the data catalog and the technology standards catalog. They are the record's architecture set; the data catalog names the migrations and the requirements catalog names the tests.

documents.title: Inception Analysis — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Inception analysis

## Current state

At inception the capability, the flow and the V1 verdict were built; the six-Gets state, the kata rows and the `kata.*` actions were absent. The project row records `needs` edges to P0, T2, S16, S17, S18, S19 and S20. The inception documents (`docs/plans/inception/T5/`) record the current state row by row with `path:symbol` citations; the delivery then built the kata rows and actions those documents designed.
## Reuse sources

The comparability rule in the benchmark improvement path, the eval versions and sign-offs, the approval policy and the seeded kata flow. Reuse is the reason the capability is one action family: a second metric, a second approval path or a second lesson store would each be a fork the analysis refuses.
## Build vs reuse

Build the kata lifecycle rows and actions; reuse the instrument, the approvals and the verdict vocabulary. Revert is built because no existing action restores a recorded base version through the target's own publish path. Lessons are deferred to the lesson register by design.
## Risks

The inception analysis named the missing six-Gets state, the benchmark-shaped measurement and the absent held-out enforcement. Delivery closed the first two and the held-out rule; the three rework findings are the residue of the third: the digest, the tenant and the drift instrument. None is a design change; each is an obligation the record already implied.

# Statement of Architecture Work

## Assignment

Deliver the architecture record for the kata capability: a procedure change measured on a held-out instrument, adopted only on a win, reverted on a regression, with the adoption decided by a person distinct from the kata's actor. The assignment is retrospective: the product shipped on issue #77 and the merges the closure review cites, and this statement records the architecture that shipped.
## Scope

The kata action family, the two kata migrations, the eval and approval reuse, and the seven A–D artefacts. Out of scope: the instruments, the lesson promotion, the development project, the andon cord and the tool platform. The phase set is A–D on the delivery ADM; the programme row carries adm_phase G and plateau capability.
## Responsibilities

The coach seat opens and measures; the kata owner sets the prediction and the instrument; the adoption approver decides keep or revert; the Architecture Board reviews the architecture record under its standing delegation; the programme owner decides the tranche. No role signs its own gate.
## Acceptance criteria

The acceptance is A1–A8 of the acceptance document, each by its test, plus the closure review's outcome-vs-acceptance table. A1–A5 are delivered; A6–A8 are the code unit's and are named open. The statement claims no tranche authority: authorisation is the programme's separate act.
## Contract

The delivery contract carries the commitments, the compliance method and the approval. The live contract row is the one the compliance review cites; this statement is its architecture half, and the two are published together so the close gate reads one consistent record.

risk.title: A measurement names an instrument that has since changed
risk.body: A completed run can be read as evidence about a version whose cases, metric or harness have moved. The risk is not that the digest is absent from the sign-off; it is that the run row does not carry it. R6 closes it with a test that edits a cited case and asserts the run still identifies what it measured.
risk.response: store the digest on the run row at completion; edits leave the recorded digest intact

risk.title: A systemic kata runs inside the tenant it coaches
risk.body: If the kata row inherits the coached tenant, the improvement can read and write the target's scope and its approvals. R7 closes it: the kata row carries tenant kata with the kata tenant's policy, and adoption needs a resolved approval by a distinct human.
risk.response: create the systemic kata under tenant kata; test the row's tenant

risk.title: A schema drift is patched without an instrument
risk.body: A 422 drift can be fixed by hand and leave no measurement, so the same drift recurs. R8 closes it: a contract-test instrument class and a kata whose threshold is the drift refusal plus a green contract test.
risk.response: open the kata from the drift signature with the contract-test instrument

issue.title: The manifest pinned active against a closed row
issue.body: The project row is closed while `acceptance/programme/T5.toml` pinned `T5-project` active, so the verifier failed the pin and the close path could not preflight. The pin now states closed, the record's measured status; the fix is recorded in the tranche's pin evidence.

issue.title: Three P1 code findings are open after delivery
issue.body: The audit registered the instrument digest, the kata tenant and the schema-drift instrument as unresolved P1 packages. They are carried by one code unit and red the receipt until they land; the closure review names them open rather than claiming them.

issue.title: The project's delivery contract was missing
issue.body: The register carried `contract_missing:T5`: no live architecture contract for the project. This pack supplies the delivery contract the factory composes and the compliance review cites.

assumption.title: The instruments stay S16–S20's
assumption.body: The kata reads eval and benchmark versions and never defines a metric. The assumption holds because the instrument rows are owned by those projects and the kata actions carry no metric writer.

assumption.title: The record's closed status is authoritative
assumption.body: The project row is closed and the closure review is the retrospective record of delivery. This pack does not re-open the project; it authors the documents the v4 close gate requires.

assumption.title: The code unit lands before the tranche exit
assumption.body: The three open findings are P1 and the receipt is red until they land. The tranche exit assumes the code unit is delivered or its claims withdrawn with evidence; nothing in this pack changes that dependency.

dependency.title: S19 supplies the eval instrument
dependency.body: The kata measures on eval versions and runs; S19 owns their creation, splits and metrics. The dependency is a `needs` edge in the project row.

dependency.title: S18 supplies the improvement verdict
dependency.body: The kept-or-reverted vocabulary and the benchmark comparison are S18's; the kata reuses them rather than writing a second verdict.

dependency.title: The tranche authorisation is #755's
dependency.body: Tranche 10 is planned; the review that records the tranche-9 decision is the only writer of its authorisation. This pack and the readiness rows do not claim it.

benefit.title: A measured improvement is auditable
benefit.body: Each kata carries its instrument, its prediction and its measurement, so an adoption can be re-read by a person who was not present. This is `B1` auditable decisions in the kata's own terms.

benefit.title: The programme improves itself on evidence
benefit.body: The kata is `B3` self-development's first instrument: a procedure change measured on a held-out instrument, adopted only on a win. The rework completes the record the benefit is measured from.

benefit.title: A regression is reverted, not remembered
benefit.body: A measured regression restores the recorded base version and records the reason, so the next unit starts from a known state rather than a warning in a document.

body.commitments: T5 delivers the kata loop over the built instrument: one kata row per open signature, a candidate with a recorded base version, a measurement on the held-out split, an adoption decided by a distinct human, a revert that restores the base, and a propagation whose targets each carry their own approval. The capability adds no metric and no second store.
body.compliance: Compliance is judged at the pinned 2026-11-28 snapshot against the record, which marks the project closed, and against SPEC_V2 §12's T5 gate. The delivered five scenarios pass by their tests; the three audit findings carried by the code unit are recorded as open, and the receipt's rework check is red until they land. The Phase-G review is recorded at level compliant for the document set it assesses.
body.approval: The adoption gate inside the capability is decided by a person distinct from the kata's actor. This contract's own approval is the Architecture Board's standing delegation, published and cited by the compliance review; the tranche authorisation is the programme owner's separate act and is not claimed here.
body.manifest: acceptance/programme/T5.toml — the manifest's project check now pins closed, the record's measured status; the remaining checks read the receipt's verdict rather than a claim.
body.acceptance_at: The 2026-11-28 retrospective snapshot, taken from the replay record at schema 110 after the pack's documents and the manifest pin were committed.
body.retrospective: This contract is authored after delivery. It records the commitments the shipped capability meets, the compliance method the receipt applies, and the open findings the record already carries; it does not re-open the delivered slice.

project_brief_output:
# Project brief

## Outcome

A procedure change is measured on a held-out instrument, adopted only when it wins, and reverted when it regresses. The outcome is true of the shipped capability and is re-read by the closure review's outcome table rather than asserted by the charter.
## Boundary

In scope: the kata lifecycle over the existing project, card, run, approval and event surfaces. Out of scope: the instruments, the lesson promotion, the development project, the andon cord and the tool platform. No second runtime, service or metric store is introduced.
## Reuse sources

The comparability rule of the benchmark improvement path, the eval versions and sign-offs, the approval policy and the seeded kata flow. Each is named in the inception analysis with its path; the delivery reuses them rather than copying them.
## Inception units

The published analysis and design pair under `docs/plans/inception/T5/`: `01-inception-analysis.md` and `02-architecture-design.md`, both published on the project before delivery. They define the rows and actions this pack records.
## Dependencies

T5 needs P0, T2, S16, S17, S18, S19 and S20. The instruments come from the eval and benchmark slices; the decision ladder and the programme spine are the other edges. None is edited by this project's units.
## Acceptance

SPEC_V2 §12's T5 gate: a procedure change measured on a held-out instrument, a regression reverted, self-approval refused, an unmeasurable kata not opened. The three audit findings are additional obligations carried by the code unit, not a redefinition of the gate.
## Capabilities

The `kata` capability owns the outcome; no other capability may fork the kata lifecycle. The capability map records the reuse edges to the instruments, approvals, lessons and development handoff.
## Plan

The plan is SPEC_V2 §12's T5 row, delivered on issue #77 and the two merges the closure review cites. The tranche plan places T5 in tranche 10 with S12; the authorisation is the tranche review's act.

# Evidence

## Claim

The kata capability delivers a measured, adopt-or-revert improvement loop with a human adoption gate and no second metric store.
## Evidence

The kata migrations 0066 and 0067, the `kata.*` action family and the integration suites kata_open, kata_measure, kata_revert, kata_adopt, kata_gets, kata_union and kata_benchmark; the merges 7e617673 (PR #636) and f8c82c68 (PR #654) recorded in the closure review.
## Verification

Run the five gate suites with `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test kata_open --test kata_measure --test kata_revert --test kata_adopt` on a checked-out main; the compile verdict is the repository's preflight. The receipt reads the pinned snapshot, not a local run.
## Links

`docs/plans/T5/closure-review.md`, `docs/plans/T5/evidence.md`, the inception set under `docs/plans/inception/T5/`, SPEC_V2 §12 and the project row's `meta.depends_on` edges.
## Gap

The three P1 code findings are open: the instrument digest a completed run must pin, the kata tenant for a systemic kata, and the contract-test instrument class for a schema drift. They are carried by one code unit and the receipt is red until they land; no other gap is claimed by the issue record.
closure: T5 is closed through the record's one gate: the project row is closed only after its charter, baseline, artefacts, registers, contract, WBS, Phase-G review, declared outputs and closure review exist, and the receipt on `acceptance/programme/T5.toml` is read against the 2026-11-28 retrospective snapshot. The closure records the delivered kata gate on its five test suites and names the three open P1 findings carried by the code unit; it claims no tranche authority, which is the tranche review's separate act.
closure_review:
# Closure Review — T5 Kata (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The delivered gate is the SPEC_V2 §12 T5 acceptance, and each row names its test: a prediction recorded before measurement (`kata_gets.rs`), the measurement on the held-out split (`kata_measure.rs`), a regression reverted and a flat result adopting nothing (`kata_revert.rs`), self-approval refused (`kata_adopt.rs`), and open/adopt refusals for an instrument-less or duplicate kata (`kata_open.rs`). All five pass on the delivered merges. The three rework findings — the run's instrument digest, the kata tenant and the schema-drift instrument — are not part of the delivered gate and remain open, carried by the code unit.
## Evidence

The migrations 0066_kata.sql and 0067_kata_gate.sql; the `kata.*` action family and its store and domain modules; the five gate suites plus kata_gets, kata_union and kata_benchmark; the merges 7e617673 (PR #636) and f8c82c68 (PR #654) in the closure review of 2026-11-25; and this pack's nine documents and seven artefacts at the pinned snapshot.
## Open items

The three P1 packages `v1-p119-1:T5`, `v1-p93-1:T5` and `v1-w1b-3:T5` are open and carried by one code unit, with test-shaped definitions of done. The receipt's rework check stays red until they land, so the tranche-10 exit waits on that unit. No other delivery item is open.
## Decision

Close the record: acceptance is met on the delivered gate by its five suites, and the open findings are a tracked P1 residue rather than a re-opening. The tranche authorisation is the programme review's separate act; this review records delivery and claims no authority over it.
